Looking at the device failure timeline from the authentication logs, I can see the owner's devices connecting from T-Mobile mobile IPs and several other addresses, and I've found the exact match for that 12:07 AM EDT screenshot—it corresponds to a 400 error with invalid credentials logged at 04:07:41Z on July 18th from IP 172.58.131.184.

The critical insight is that there are no device login attempts whatsoever after the 04:12Z repair window; the owner's last attempt was the failed one at 04:07:41Z, so they haven't retried since the fix was applied. That explains why the device failure can't be reproduced now—the server is accepting the correct password, but the device simply hasn't tried logging in again. The request ID is 019f7368-93b9-77d6-a15c-8cba3e78fe4b, and the POST to the token endpoint returned a 400 with invalid_credentials. The login bypasses the main API and goes straight to Supabase Auth, so their service logs are the authoritative backend record — showing the request completed in about 125 milliseconds with a password hash mismatch at that time, before the repair happened.

No ban or rate limiting was in effect. The failed attempt never created a JWT or session, and the sessions table stayed empty until after the repair when server-side grants started working. The device was definitely on production hitting the correct project. The reason the device can't reproduce the failure now is that the stored password genuinely didn't match at 04:07:41Z — I confirmed the same request would fail from anywhere at that time, but after the 04:12Z repair it succeeds. The auth logs show zero login attempts from the device after the repair, meaning the phone hasn't retried since then.
